newsitem.title: IRAQ: Oil companies flock to Baghdad to buy crude.
newsitem.headline: Oil companies flock to Baghdad to buy crude.

text.p: An Iraqi oil official said Thursday that foreign firms were flocking to Baghdad to finalise deals for the purchase of Iraqi crude under Baghdad's oil-for-food agreement with the United Nations.

"Many companies arrived today and many more are on their way. We wrote to all those who dealt with us in the past and the response has been very positive," an official of the State Organisation for the Marketing of Oil said, refusing to be named.
He said representives from France's Elf Aquitaine and Japan's Mitsubishi were among those companies in Baghdad seeking shipments of Iraqi crude.

"Not only Elf and Mitsubishi, which could be the first to load Iraqi crude. There are many other firms in Baghdad," he said. "Demand for our oil is much higher than what we could be allowed to export under the deal with the U.N."

He said the quantity Iraq would be allowed to export depended on prevalent prices, whose surge recenly lowered the limited amounts Iraq can export from about 800,000 barrels to about 550,000 barrels per day in six months.
